questions.prompt: Identify one component of a wireframe.
questions.markSchemeHint: Navigation bar/menu, image/video placeholder, text placeholder, buttons/icons, header/footer, annotations/labels, layout boxes.

questions.prompt: Unix is an example of which of the following?
questions.markSchemeHint: C) Operating system (1 mark).

questions.prompt: Identify two interaction methods that can be used with a mobile device.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: touch, voice, gesture, stylus/pen, tilt/motion sensors, on-screen keyboard.

questions.prompt: Percentage is an example of which data type?
questions.markSchemeHint: Numeric (or Real/Decimal).

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence:
The alphanumeric data type can include [Blank 1] and [Blank 2].
questions.markSchemeHint: Letters (characters/text) (1) and Numbers (digits) (1) — also accept symbols/spaces.

questions.scenarioContext: One secondary data collection method is a magazine.
questions.prompt: Identify two other secondary data collection methods.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: books, websites/internet, newspapers, government reports/census data, journals, existing databases/company records.

questions.prompt: What does NAS stand for?
questions.markSchemeHint: Network Attached Storage.

questions.prompt: Which type of hacker gains unauthorised access to a digital system with malicious intent?
questions.markSchemeHint: A) Black hat (1 mark).

questions.prompt: Link the impact of a cyber-security attack to its correct description. (You will only use two types of impact.)
matchingLeft: The taking of data at rest or in transit.
Stolen personal data is used to commit fraud.
questions.markSchemeHint: Data Theft -> The taking of data at rest or in transit (1); Identity Theft -> Stolen personal data is used to commit fraud (1).

questions.prompt: Which secure data destruction method replaces old data with new data?
questions.markSchemeHint: Overwriting (or wiping/shredding software).

questions.prompt: Identify one type of Internet of Everything (IoE) digital interactivity.
questions.markSchemeHint: Device to device (D2D), Human to device (H2D), or Device to human (D2H) / Machine to machine (M2M).

questions.scenarioContext: A bank is launching a new savings account. Customers can access the savings account online using an app or through the website of the bank. The app and website will use the same human computer interface (HCI). A laptop could be used to access the savings account HCI.
questions.prompt: Explain two characteristics of a laptop that make it appropriate to access the savings account HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: 2 marks each (characteristic + explanation): larger screen makes financial tables/details easier to read; full physical keyboard/trackpad improves accuracy when typing account details; portable/battery-powered for banking anywhere; built-in Wi-Fi for online access.

questions.prompt: Identify two digital devices other than a laptop that can be used to access the savings account HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: smartphone, tablet, desktop PC, smartwatch.

questions.scenarioContext: The bank's savings account app and website will use the same HCI.
questions.prompt: Identify two advantages to customers of the bank using a HCI for the savings account.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: 24/7 access from home without visiting a branch, easy/intuitive navigation, consistent experience across app and website, instant balance/transaction checking, accessibility options.

questions.prompt: Identify two disadvantages to customers of the bank using a HCI for the savings account.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: requires internet access/digital device, security/phishing risks, difficult for less tech-literate/elderly customers, no face-to-face staff support, downtime prevents access.

questions.scenarioContext: Designing the bank savings account HCI.
questions.prompt: Explain why the memory resource of the hardware should be considered when a HCI is being designed.
questions.markSchemeHint: If the HCI uses too much RAM/memory (e.g., heavy graphics/animations) (1), older or lower-spec customer devices may lag, freeze, or crash when accessing their account (1).

questions.scenarioContext: A bank is launching a new savings account. The first part of the HCI will allow users to log-in to their new savings account.
questions.prompt:
Create a mind map to plan the log-in screen of the HCI.
Marks will be awarded for: content; layout.
questions.markSchemeHint: Up to 4 marks Content (central node 'Savings Account Log-In', branches for Inputs like Username/Account No./Password/Memorable info, Security like 2FA/Biometrics, Help/Forgotten password, House style/Accessibility, Navigation/Submit button) and up to 4 marks Layout (clear central idea, organised branches and sub-branches, concise keywords, easy to follow hierarchy).

questions.scenarioContext: The HCI for the savings account will be tested before going live.
questions.prompt: Explain the purpose of carrying out technical testing on the savings account HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: To check the system works correctly under the hood—e.g., links, validation rules, security, calculations, and performance/load handling (1) so bugs/vulnerabilities are fixed before real customers use it (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Technical testing of the bank savings account HCI.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to the bank of carrying out technical testing.
questions.markSchemeHint: Advantage (2): identifies errors/security flaws early, preventing costly post-launch failures, data breaches, or reputational damage. Disadvantage (2): costs money/specialist staff time and can delay the launch date of the savings account.

questions.scenarioContext: As part of the testing process user testing will be carried out.
questions.prompt: Identify and explain one example of user testing that would be carried out on the savings account HCI.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark valid user test (usability testing, accessibility testing, beta testing, acceptance testing) + 1 mark explanation linked to savings account customers checking ease of use/requirements.

questions.scenarioContext:
An example of the stored savings account data:
• Account number: KFS0012
• Name of account holder: Emma Riley
• Account holder date of birth: 26/02/2016
• Amount paid in (£): 10.50
• Amount taken out (£): 0.00
• Balance: 125.00
• Contact email address: EPR@phmail.co.uk
questions.prompt: Complete the table to show the data types used when storing the savings account data. Justify your choices.
questions.markSchemeHint: 3 marks per row (1 data type + 2 justification): Account number -> Alphanumeric/Text (contains letters KFS and digits 0012, preserves leading zeros); Date of birth -> Date (stores DD/MM/YYYY format allowing age verification/date validation); Balance -> Currency (or Real/Decimal) (stores monetary value to 2 decimal places for financial calculations).

questions.scenarioContext: Storing personal data of savings account holders.
questions.prompt: Identify the legislation that relates to the storing of personal data.
questions.markSchemeHint: Data Protection Act (2018) / UK GDPR.

questions.scenarioContext: The bank will use a range of logical prevention measures to protect the savings account data.
questions.prompt: Explain how using secure back-ups can help protect the savings account data.
questions.markSchemeHint: Creates duplicate copies of account data stored securely/off-site (1) so if original data is lost, corrupted, or encrypted by ransomware, the bank can restore accurate customer balances (1).

questions.prompt: Identify two other logical prevention measures that the bank could use to protect the savings account data.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: encryption, firewall, strong passwords/usernames, two-factor authentication (2FA), anti-malware/anti-virus, access levels/permissions, software updates/patching.

questions.scenarioContext: After setting up their new savings account, all account holders are contacted to explain how to protect their savings account details.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage to the bank of using email to distribute this information to customers.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark point + 1 mark expansion: cheap/no printing or postage costs; instant delivery to all account holders at once; can include attachments/links to security guides; automated mail-merge.

questions.scenarioContext: The bank uses social media to provide more information about cyber-security threats and the logical prevention measures that account users could use.
questions.markSchemeHint: OCR 9-mark Level of Response (L1: 1–3, L2: 4–6, L3: 7–9). Purpose: share timely public updates, raise awareness, engage interactively with followers. Advantages: wide reach, low cost, rapid alerts about active scams/phishing, multimedia tips (short videos/infographics), shareable. Disadvantages: scammers can impersonate bank accounts/reply with phishing links, public complaints damage trust, not all customers use social media, character/detail limits, moderation costs. Reasoned conclusion.

questions.scenarioContext: The bank suffered a cyber-security attack when the savings account data was accessed by a hacker.
questions.prompt: Identify two types of malware that could have been used.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: Spyware, Trojan Horse, Worm, Virus, Ransomware, Rootkit, Keylogger, Adware.
